descriptionChirho: The primary Hifil sense of ירה I meaning to teach, instruct, or give instruction; consistently glossed with Arabic عَلَّمَ (teach), Korean 가르치다 (teach), Swahili -fundisha (teach), Spanish enseñar (teach), and Hindi सिखाना (teach), across all finite verbal inflections including imperfect, perfect, imperative, infinitive, and consecutive forms — the core pedagogical sense of the causative stem.

The substantivized Hifil participle of ירה I functioning as the noun 'teacher' (מורה); distinguished from the active verbal 'teach' sense by nominal syntax and glosses such as Arabic مُعَلِّم (teacher), Spanish maestro (teacher/master), Swahili mwalimu (teacher), Korean 스승 (master/teacher), and Hindi शिक्षक (teacher), indicating a person rather than an action.

An extended Hifil sense of ירה I meaning to show, point out, or direct, where the causative force implies guiding or indicating rather than formal instruction; distinguished by glosses such as English 'showed him,' 'pointing,' 'direct,' Spanish mostró (showed), Hindi दिखाया/बताना (showed/told), Arabic أَرَاهُ/يُشِيرُ (showed him / points), and Swahili -onyesha/-arifu (show / inform).

The primary sense of ירה II meaning to shoot arrows or projectiles, appearing in both Qal and Hifil stems; consistently glossed with Arabic رَمَى (throw/shoot), Korean 쏘다 (shoot), Swahili -piga mishale (shoot arrows), Spanish disparar (shoot/fire), and Hindi चलाना (discharge/shoot), encompassing all finite verbal forms of projectile launching in military and narrative contexts.

The substantivized participle of ירה II functioning as the noun 'archer' or 'shooter' (plural הַיּוֹרִים / הָרֹמִים); distinguished by nominal syntax with the article, glosses such as English 'the archers / the shooters,' Spanish los arqueros / los flecheros (the archers), Arabic الرُّمَاة (the archers), Korean 활쏘는자들 (those who shoot bows), and Swahili wapiga mishale (arrow shooters).

The Qal sense of ירה II meaning to cast, throw, or hurl objects (not specifically arrows); distinguished from the 'shoot' sense by objects such as bodies or lots rather than projectiles, with glosses such as English 'cast / threw / laid,' Spanish arrojó / lancé / echará (threw / cast), Arabic طَرَحَ / أَلْقَى (threw / cast), Korean 던지다 (throw), and Swahili -tupa (throw/cast).

The Nifal (simple passive) of ירה II meaning to be shot or struck with an arrow; glossed as English 'he shall be shot,' Spanish será arrojado (he will be cast/shot), Arabic يُرْمَى (he is thrown/shot), Korean 쏘아 맞으리라 (will be hit by shooting), and Swahili atapigwa kwa mshale (he will be struck with an arrow).

A distinct Hifil sense of ירה (possibly related to ירד 'descend') meaning to send rain or to water, used of God causing rain to fall; glossed as English 'watering / rains,' Spanish riega / llueva (irrigates / may it rain), Arabic يَسقي / يُمطِرَ (waters / sends rain), Korean 적시는 / 비를 내리시리라 (soaking / will send rain), and Swahili -nyesha (cause rain).
